text: When your child (13–15) asks, “Why do we pray?” — don’t say, “Because Allah commanded it.” Say, “I feel peace when I am close to Allah.”

review_defects.why: The Arabic 'قال' means 'said', not 'commanded'. The English adds the notion of a command, which is not present in the original and changes the tone of the advice.

review_defects.english: I feel peace when I am close to Allah
review_defects.why: The Arabic 'الراحة' means 'comfort' or 'rest', not 'peace' (which is usually 'سلام'). The nuance is slightly altered.
